analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md changes the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph (lines 334-339) about Autopilot placement holds. docs/architecture/inference.md changes its date (line 3) and adds a failure-mode table row near line 2316. No code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, authorization, or encryption behavior is changed.

The new text says an unexpired Autopilot hold removes a slot from eviction snapshots (`ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots`) and gives its weights no `free_for_load_gb` reclaim credit (`autopilotHeldWeightBytes`). A load that fits only by evicting a held slot then fails with the ordinary slot or insufficient-memory refusal. This describes provider-local availability and memory-admission behavior; it is not a new security boundary. The reviewed excerpts do not show how long holds last or who can create them, so the documented behavior could let held slots crowd out loads (T-029-style availability). The remaining integration question is whether hold creation and expiry are bounded and coordinator-authorized. That is a contract in code and in model-autopilot.md, neither of which was supplied, so I am not recording it as a finding.

I checked the existing text for threat-model conflicts. The Nemotron Super and cross-repository references to platform admission are pre-existing, and the immutable platform links are unchanged. The edits contradict none of the threat model assets, trust boundaries, or T-041 prefix-cache claims. No finding.
